name: 2026-11-17-nm36-distill
registered: 2026-11-17, before nm36 started training; the pushed commit that adds this file is the record
question: Does training nm25 towards search's improved policy (expert iteration) make a stronger network than nm25?

run.nm36: init blueprint/nm25/checkpoint.pt; nm25's settings (--tourney --menu mtt --depths 10,25 --ante 1 --short 0.5 --no-open-limp --pg neurd --neurd-beta 4 --kl 0.3 --entropy 0.04 --pool reg,reg,tag,maniac,station --pool-share 0.5 --exploit-share 0.25 --exploit-reset 60 --chunks 4 --batch 16384); --distill blueprint/distill_nm25 (600,000 positions from nm25 self-play, each labelled by search with 2,048 deals: Q per legal move and nm25's policy) --distill-tau 1.0 --distill-weight 1.0 --distill-batch 4096; 6 hours on the PRO 6000; the averaged network is compared

primary.metric: sequential duplicate match, nm36 in each seat against 8 x nm25 (scripts/seqtest.py): up to 40,000 deals in 8 looks, O'Brien-Fleming at alpha 0.05 (C 2.0696), equivalence margin 0.5 bb/100
primary.decision: nm36 is better if the match stops for a difference with nm36 ahead; equivalent or behind: not adopted

secondary.exploiter: 30-minute exploiter against nm36; it must not exceed nm25's (+0.2 [-0.4, +0.7]) by more than 1 bb/100 for nm36 to be adopted
secondary.copy_check: the exploiter's minute-0 reading (nm36 against itself) must be 0 within its interval
secondary.sense: ninemax_sense.py and ninemax_postflop.py pass counts; reported (the tight button steal of nm25 is watched)
secondary.search: the same sequential match for nm36 + search against nm25 + search is a follow-up, not part of the decision

not_allowed: changing the tau, weight, data, budget, metric or decision rule after seeing any nm36 result; re-running the match and keeping the better reading
